## Rule 83.15

## SECTION I SCOPE AND INTERPRETATION

## Scope and interpretation

## 83.1

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (1) This Part contains general rules about writs and warrants as follows—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (a) Section II relates to writs and warrants;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (b) Section III relates to writs only; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (c) Section IV relates to warrants only.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (2) In this Part—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (a) ‘the Act’ means the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007 1 ;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (b) ‘the creditor’ means a person who has obtained or who is entitled to enforce a judgment or order;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (c) ‘the debtor’ means a person against whom a judgment or order was given or made;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (d) ‘enforcement agent’ has the meaning given in paragraph 2(1) of Schedule 12;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (e) ‘enforcement officer’ means an individual who is authorised to act as an enforcement officer under Schedule 7 to the Courts Act 2003 2 ;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (f) ‘relevant enforcement officer’ means—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (i) in relation to a writ of execution or a writ of control which is directed to a single enforcement officer, that officer; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (ii) in relation to a writ of execution or writ of control which is directed to two or more enforcement officers, the officer to whom the writ is allocated;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (g) ‘Schedule 12’ means Schedule 12 to the Act 3 ;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (h) ‘TCG procedure’ means the procedure in Schedule 12 to take control of goods and sell them to recover a sum in accordance with that Schedule and regulations made under it;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (i) ‘TCG Regulations’ means the Taking Control of Goods Regulations 2013 4 ;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (j) ‘warrant of control’ is to be construed in accordance with section 62(4) of the Act;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (k) ‘writ of control’ is to be construed in accordance with section 62(4) of the Act;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (l) ‘writ of execution’ includes—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (i) a writ of possession;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (ii) a writ of delivery;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (iii) a writ of sequestration;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (iv) a writ of fieri facias de bonis ecclesiasticis,

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] and any further writ in aid of any such writs, but does not include a writ of control.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.1] (3) This Part does not apply where an application is made seeking confiscation of assets as a punishment for contempt of court. Any such application must be made under Part 81 and not under this Part.

## SECTION II WRITS AND WARRANTS

## 83.2

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (1)  This rule applies to—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (a) writs and warrants of control;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (b) writs of execution;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (c) warrants of delivery;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (d) warrants of possession.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (2) A writ or warrant to which this rule applies is referred to in this rule as a ‘relevant writ or warrant’.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (3) A relevant writ or warrant must not be issued without the permission of the court where—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (a) six years or more have elapsed since the date of the judgment or order;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (b) any change has taken place, whether by death or otherwise, in the parties—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (i) entitled to enforce the judgment or order; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (ii) liable to have it enforced against them;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (c) the judgment or order is against the assets of a deceased person coming into the hands of that person’s executors or administrators after the date of the judgment or order, and it is sought to issue execution against such assets;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (d) any goods to be seized under a relevant writ or warrant are in the hands of a receiver appointed by a court or sequestrator;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (e) under the judgment or order, any person is entitled to a remedy subject to the fulfilment of any condition, and it is alleged that the condition has been fulfilled (other than where non-compliance with the terms of suspension of enforcement of the judgment or order is the failure to pay money);

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (f) the permission sought is for a writ of control or writ of execution, and that writ is to be in aid of another writ of control or execution; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (g) an application is made for a writ of sequestration.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (Rule 83.14A makes provision for applications for permission to issue a writ of sequestration.)

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (4) An application for permission may be made in accordance with Part 23 and must—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (a)identify the judgment or order to which the application relates;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (b) if the judgment or order is for the payment of money, state the amount originally due and, if different, the amount due at the date the application notice is filed;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (c) where the case falls within paragraph (3)(a), state the reasons for the delay in enforcing the judgment or order;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (d) where the case falls within paragraph (3)(b), state the change which has taken place in the parties entitled or liable to execution since the date of the judgment or order;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (e) where the case falls within paragraph (3)(c) or (d), state that a demand to satisfy the judgment or order was made on the person liable to satisfy it and that that person has refused or failed to do so;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (f) give such other information as is necessary to satisfy the court that the applicant is entitled to proceed to execution on the judgment or order, and that the person against whom it is sought to issue execution is liable to execution on it.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (5) An application for permission may be made without notice being served on any other party unless the court directs otherwise.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (6) If because of one event, an applicant seeks permission under paragraph (3)(b) to enforce more than one judgment or order, the applicant need only make one application for permission.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (7) Where paragraph (6) applies—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (a) a schedule must be attached to the application for permission, specifying all the judgments or orders in respect of which the application for permission is made; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (b) if the application notice is directed to be served on any person, it need set out only such part of the application as affects that person.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (7A) Where—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (a) the court grants permission, under this rule or otherwise, for the issue of a writ of execution or writ of control (‘the permission order’); and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (b) the writ is not issued within one year after the date of the permission order,

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] the permission order will cease to have effect.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (7B) Where a permission order has ceased to have effect, the court may grant a fresh permission order.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.2] (8) Paragraph (3) is without prejudice to section 2 of the Reserve and Auxiliary Forces (Protection of Civil Interests) Act 1951 5 and any enactment, rule or direction by virtue of which a person is required to obtain the permission of the court for the issue of a warrant or to proceed to execution or otherwise to the enforcement of a judgment or order.

## 83.3

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (1)  This rule applies to—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (a) writs of execution;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (b) warrants of possession; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (c) warrants of delivery,

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] other than writs of execution or warrants that confer a power to use the TCG procedure.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (2) A writ or warrant to which this rule applies is referred to in this rule as a ‘relevant writ or warrant’, ‘relevant writ’ or ‘relevant warrant’ as appropriate.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (3) Subject to paragraph (4), for the purposes of execution, a writ or warrant will be valid for the period of 12 months beginning with the date of its issue.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (4) The court may extend the relevant writ or warrant from time to time for a period of 12 months at any one time.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (5) If the application is made before the expiry of the period of 12 months, the period of extension will begin on the day after the expiry.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (6) If the application is made after the expiry of the period of 12 months, any period of extension will begin on any day after the expiry that the court may allow.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (7) Before a relevant writ that has been extended is executed—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (a) the court will seal the writ; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (b) the applicant for the extension order must serve a notice sealed as described in subparagraph (a) on the relevant enforcement officer informing that officer of the making of the extension order and the date of that order.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (8) In relation to a relevant warrant, the court will endorse the warrant with a note of the renewal or extension.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (9) Irrespective of whether it has been extended under paragraph (4)—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (a) the priority of a relevant writ will be determined by reference to the time it is originally received by the person who is under a duty to endorse it; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (b) the priority of a relevant warrant will be determined by reference to the date on which it was originally issued.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (10) The production of the following will be evidence that the relevant writ or warrant has been extended—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (a) the writ sealed in accordance with paragraph (7)(a);

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (b) the notice sealed in accordance with paragraph (7)(b);

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (c) the warrant endorsed in accordance with paragraph (8).

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.3] (11) If, during the validity of a relevant writ, a person makes an application under Part 85 in relation to an execution under that writ, the validity of the writ will be extended until the expiry of 12 months from the conclusion of the proceedings under Part 85.

## Writs and warrants conferring a power to use the TCG procedure – duration and priority

## 83.4

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (1)  This rule applies to—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (a) a writ of control;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (b) a warrant of control; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (c) any other writ or warrant that confers power to use the TCG procedure.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (2) A writ or warrant to which this rule applies is referred to in this rule as a ‘relevant writ or warrant’, ‘relevant writ’ or ‘relevant warrant’ as appropriate.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (3) A relevant writ or warrant will be valid for the period in which an enforcement agent may take control of the goods in question, as specified in regulation 9(1) of the TCG Regulations.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (4) If a period in which to take control of goods is extended by the court under regulation 9(3) of the TCG Regulations, the validity of the relevant writ or warrant will be extended for the same period.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (Rule 84.5 contains provisions about applications to the court requesting a time extension.)

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (5) Irrespective of whether it has been extended under regulation 9(3) of the TCG Regulations—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (a) the priority of a relevant writ will be determined by reference to the time it is originally received by the person who is under a duty to endorse it; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (b) the priority of a relevant warrant will be determined by reference to the date on which it was originally issued.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (6) The production of—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (a) the extension order granted under regulation 9(3) of the TCG Regulations, or a copy of it; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (b) the relevant writ or warrant endorsed in accordance with rule 84.5(3)(b), or a copy of it,

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] will be evidence that the writ or warrant has been extended.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.4] (7) If, during the validity of a relevant writ or warrant, a person makes an application under Part 85 in relation to goods taken into control under that writ or warrant, the validity of the writ or warrant will be extended until the expiry of 12 months from the conclusion of the proceedings under Part 85.

## Writs and warrants – separate enforcement of costs

## 83.5

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (1)  Where—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (a) judgment is given or an order made for—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (i) payment of a sum otherwise than by instalments (‘the sum’); and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (ii) costs to be assessed; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (b) default is made in payment of the sum before the costs have been assessed,

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] a writ of control or warrant of control (as appropriate) may be issued for the recovery of the sum.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (2) If—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (a) paragraph (1) applies;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (b) a writ or warrant is issued for the recovery of the sum;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (c) the costs are assessed; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (d) default is made in payment of the costs,

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] a separate writ of control or warrant of control may be issued for the recovery of the costs.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (3) A party entitled to enforce a judgment or order of the High Court for—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (a) the delivery of any property, other than money; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (b) possession of any property,

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] may issue a separate writ of control to enforce payment of any damages or costs awarded to that party by that judgment or order.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.5] (4) A party entitled to enforce a judgment or order of the County Court by warrant of delivery may issue a separate warrant of control to enforce payment of any damages or costs awarded to that party by that judgment or order.

## Writs and warrants – levying execution on certain days

## 83.6

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.6] (1)  This rule applies to writs and warrants other than—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.6] (a) writs of control;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.6] (b) warrants of control; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.6] (c) writs or warrants in relation to an Admiralty claim in rem.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.6] (2)  Where a writ or warrant is not a writ of control or warrant of control but nevertheless confers the power to use the TCG procedure, this rule applies to the parts of the writ or warrant that do not confer the power to use the TCG Procedure.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.6] (3)  Unless the court orders otherwise, a writ or warrant to enforce a judgment or order must not be executed on a Sunday, Good Friday or Christmas Day.

## Writs of control and warrants – power to stay execution or grant other relief

## 83.7

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (1)  At the time that a judgment or order for payment of money is made or granted, or at any time thereafter, the debtor or other party liable to execution of a writ of control or a warrant may apply to the court for a stay of execution.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (2) The power of the court to stay execution of a warrant of control may be exercised by a District Judge, or a court officer where paragraph (10) applies, and the power of the court to stay execution of any other warrant or of a writ of control may be exercised by a Master or District Judge.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (3) Where the application for a stay of execution is made on the grounds of the applicant’s inability to pay, the witness statement required by paragraph (6)(b) must disclose the debtor’s means.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (4) If the court is satisfied that—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (a) there are special circumstances which render it inexpedient to enforce the judgment or order; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (b) the applicant is unable from any reason to pay the money,

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] then, notwithstanding anything in paragraph (5) or (6), the court may by order stay the execution of the judgment or order, either absolutely or for such period and subject to such conditions as the court thinks fit.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (5) An application under this rule, if not made at the time the judgment is given or order made—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (a) must be made in accordance with Part 23, as modified by paragraphs (6) to (14); and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (b) may be made even if the party liable to execution did not acknowledge service of the claim form or serve a defence or take any previous part in the proceedings.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (6) The grounds on which an application under this rule is made must—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (a) be set out in the application notice; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (b) be supported by a witness statement made by or on behalf of the applicant substantiating the grounds.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (7) Paragraphs (8) to (15) apply to applications in the County Court.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (8) Where the debtor makes an application in the County Court, the court will—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (a) send the creditor a copy of the debtor’s application (and statement of means); and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (b) require the creditor to notify the court in writing whether or not the creditor objects to the application, within 14 days of service of the notification, giving reasons for any objection the creditor may have to the granting of the application.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (9) If the creditor does not notify the court of any objection within the time stated, the court officer may make an order suspending the warrant on terms of payment.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (10) Upon receipt of a notice by the creditor under paragraph (8)(b), the court officer may, if the creditor agrees, or objects only to the terms offered, determine the date and rate of payment and make an order suspending the warrant on terms of payment.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (11) Any party affected by an order made under paragraph (10) may, within 14 days of service of the order on that party and giving reasons, apply on notice for the order to be reconsidered.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (12) If a party applies for the order to be reconsidered, the court will—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (a) fix a day for the hearing of the application before the District Judge; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (b) give to the creditor and the debtor not less than 8 days’ notice of the day so fixed.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (13) On hearing an application under paragraph (11), the District Judge may confirm the order or set it aside and make such new order as the court thinks fit.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (14) Where the creditor states in the notice under paragraph (8)(b) that the creditor wishes the enforcement agent to proceed to execute the warrant, the court will—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (a) fix a day for a hearing before the District Judge of the debtor’s application; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (b) give to the creditor and to the debtor not less than 2 days’ notice of the day so fixed.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.7] (15) Where an order is made by the District Judge suspending a warrant of execution, the debtor may be ordered to pay the costs of the warrant and any fees or expenses incurred before its suspension and the order may authorise the sale of a sufficient portion of any goods seized to cover such costs, fees and expenses and the expenses of sale.

## Writs and warrants – information about execution of the writ or warrant

## 83.8

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8] (1)  If the creditor or debtor serves notice on the enforcement agent or enforcement officer requiring reasonable information about the execution of a writ or warrant, the enforcement agent or enforcement officer must send such information to the creditor or debtor within 7 days of service of the notice.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8] (2) If the enforcement agent or enforcement officer fails to comply with the notice, the party who served the notice may apply to the court for an order directing the enforcement agent or enforcement officer to comply with the notice.

## Notice of execution of writs and warrants of possession

## 83.8A

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (1) This rule applies to—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (a) writs of possession; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (b) warrants of possession,

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] other than writs and warrants excluded by paragraph (6).

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (2) Subject to paragraph (5)—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (a) a notice of eviction must be delivered to the premises not less than 14 days before the writ or warrant is executed; but

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (b) if full execution of the writ or warrant has not taken place on the day specified in a notice of eviction delivered pursuant to sub-paragraph (a) relating to the writ or warrant, or on or by the day or days specified in any further notice of eviction or further notices of eviction delivered pursuant to this sub-paragraph relating to the writ or warrant, a further notice of eviction must be delivered to the premises not less than 7 days before the writ or warrant is or is further executed.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (3) The notice of eviction referred to in paragraph (2)(a) and any further notice of eviction or further notices of eviction referred to in paragraph (2)(b) must each must—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (a) be addressed to—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (i) all persons against whom the possession order was made; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (ii) “any other occupiers”; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (b) be in the relevant form prescribed by Practice Direction 83.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (4) The notice of eviction and any further notice of eviction or further notices of eviction must each must be delivered by—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (a) inserting it through the letter box in a sealed transparent envelope; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (b) if that is not practicable—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (i) attaching a copy to the main door or some other part of the land so that it is clearly visible; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (ii) if that is not practicable, placing stakes in the land in places where they are clearly visible and attaching to each stake a copy of the notice in a sealed transparent envelope.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (5) The court may(at the request of any person)—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (a) dispense with the requirement to deliver a notice of eviction or any further notice of eviction or any further notices of eviction; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (b) extend or shorten the time by which a notice of eviction or any further notice of eviction or any further notices of eviction must be delivered,

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] but may not exercise its powers under sub-paragraph (b) so as to postpone the date of execution of any writ or warrant of possession beyond the last date permitted for that purpose by or under any enactment.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.8A] (6) This rule does not apply to writs or warrants of possession to enforce possession orders against trespassers, other than possession orders against persons who entered or remained on the premises with the consent of a person who, at the time consent was given, had an immediate right to possession of the premises.

## SECTION III WRITS

## Issue of writs of execution and writs of control

## 83.9

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (1)  In this rule ‘the appropriate office’ means—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (a) where the proceedings in which execution is to issue are in a District Registry, that Registry;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (b) where the proceedings are in the Principal Registry of the Family Division, that Registry

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (c) where the proceedings are Admiralty proceedings or commercial proceedings which are not in a District Registry, the Admiralty and Commercial Registry;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (ca) where the proceedings are in the Chancery Division, Chancery Chambers;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (d) in any other case, the Central Office of the Senior Courts.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (2) Issue of a writ of execution or control takes place on its being sealed by a court officer of the appropriate office.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (3) Before a writ is issued a request for its issue must be filed.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (4) The request must be signed—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (a) by the person entitled to execution, if acting in person; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (b) by or on behalf of the solicitor of the person entitled to execution.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (5) Subject to paragraph (5A), the writ will not be sealed unless at the time it is presented for sealing—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (a) the person presenting the writ produces—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (i) the judgment or order on which the writ is to issue, or an office copy of it;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (ii) where permission was required for the writ to be issued, the order granting such permission or evidence of the granting of it;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (iii) where judgment on failure to acknowledge service has been entered against a State, as defined in section 14 of the State Immunity Act 1978 6 , evidence that the State has been served in accordance with rule 40.10 and that the judgment has taken effect; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (b) the court officer authorised to seal it is satisfied that the period, if any, specified in the judgment or order for the payment of any money or the doing of any other act under the judgment or order has expired.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (5A) Where a request is made for a writ of possession to enforce a notice under section 33D of the Immigration Act 2014(4) (termination of agreement where all occupiers disqualified), a copy of that notice must be filed with the request instead of the judgment or order required by paragraph (5)(a)(i).

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.9] (6) Every writ of execution or control will bear the date of the day on which it is issued.

## Writs of control and writs of delivery – description of parties

## 83.10

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.10] (1)  This rule applies where the name or address of the creditor or debtor as given in the request for the issue of the following differs from that person’s name or address in the judgment or order sought to be enforced—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.10] (a) a writ of control;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.10] (b) writ of delivery.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.10] (2) If the creditor files a witness statement that satisfies the court officer that the name or address as given in the request is applicable to the person concerned, the creditor or the debtor will be described in the writ as ‘CD of [name and address as given in the request] suing [or sued] as AD of [name and address in the judgment or order]’.

## Writs relating to ecclesiastical property

## 83.11

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.11] (1)  In this rule, ‘a writ relating to ecclesiastical property’ means—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.11] (a) a writ of fieri facias de bonis ecclesiasticis; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.11] (b) a writ of sequestrari de bonis ecclesiasticis.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.11] (2) This rule applies where it appears upon the return of any writ of control that the person against whom the writ was issued—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.11] (a) has no goods or chattels in the district of the relevant enforcement officer; but

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.11] (b) is the incumbent of a benefice named in the return.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.11] (3) After the writ and return have been filed, the party by whom the writ of control was issued may issue a writ relating to ecclesiastical property.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.11] (4) Any such writ must be directed and delivered to the bishop of the diocese within which that benefice is, to be executed by that bishop.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.11] (5) The only fees allowed to the bishop or diocesan officer for the execution of the writ are those authorised by or under any enactment, including any measure of the General Synod.

## 83.12

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (1) This rule applies in relation to writs that do not confer a power to use the TCG procedure.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (2) A court order under paragraph 10 of Schedule 7 to the Courts Act 2003 7 that a sale of goods seized under an execution may be made otherwise than by public auction may be made on the application of—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (a) the person at whose instance the writ of execution under which the sale is to be made was issued;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (b) the person against whom that writ was issued (in this rule referred to as ‘the judgment debtor’); or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (c) if the writ was directed to one or more enforcement officers, the relevant enforcement officer.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (3) Such an application must be made in accordance with Part 23.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (4) Where the applicant for an order under this rule is not the enforcement officer, the enforcement officer must, on the demand of the applicant, send to the applicant a list, stating—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (a) whether the enforcement officer has notice of the issue of another writ or writs of execution against the goods of the judgment debtor; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (b) so far as is known to the enforcement officer, the name and address of every creditor who has obtained the issue of another such writ of execution.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (5) Where the enforcement officer is the applicant, the enforcement officer must prepare such a list.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (6) Not less than 3 days before the hearing, the applicant must serve the application notice on each of the other persons by whom the application might have been made and on every person named in the list prepared under paragraph (4) or (5).

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (7) Service of the application notice on a person named in the list prepared under paragraph (4) or (5) is notice to that person for the purpose of paragraph 10(3) of Schedule 7 to the Courts Act 2003.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (8) The applicant must produce the list prepared under paragraph (4) or (5) to the court on the hearing of the application.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.12] (9) Every person on whom the application notice was served may attend and be heard on the hearing of the application.

## Enforcement in the High Court of a judgment or order for possession of land

## 83.13

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (1)  A judgment or order for the giving of possession of land may be enforced in the High Court by one or more of the following means—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (a) writ of possession;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (b) proceedings for contempt of court under Part 81;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (c) where no such proceedings are brought, by a writ of sequestration.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (2) No writ of possession to enforce a notice under section 33D of the Immigration Act 2014 may be issued without the permission of the court.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (3) No writ of possession against a trespasser may be issued after the expiry of 3 months from the date of the order without the permission of the court.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (4) Unless the court otherwise directs, an application for permission under paragraph (3) may be made without notice to any other party.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (4A) The court’s permission to issue a writ of restitution in aid of a writ of possession is required whether or not permission was required for the writ of possession.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (5) An application for a writ of possession may be made without notice.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (6) The person applying for a writ of possession must file a certificate that the land which is the subject of the judgment or order has not been vacated.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (7) A writ of possession may include provision for enforcing the payment of any money adjudged or ordered to be paid by the judgment or order which is to be enforced by the writ.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (8) In a case to which paragraph (7) applies or where an order for possession has been suspended on terms as to payment of a sum of money by instalments, the person applying for a writ of possession must certify—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (a) the amount of money remaining due under the judgment or order; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.13] (b) that the whole or part of any instalment due remains unpaid.

## Enforcement in the High Court of a judgment or order for delivery of goods

## 83.14

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14] (1)  A judgment or order for the delivery of any goods which does not give a person against whom the judgment is given or order made the alternative of paying the assessed value of the goods may be enforced in the High Court by one or more of the following means—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14] (a) writ of delivery to recover the goods without alternative provision for recovery of the assessed value of those goods (‘writ of specific delivery’);

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14] (b) proceedings for contempt of court under Part 81;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14] (c) where no such proceedings are brought, by a writ of sequestration.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14] (2) A judgment or order for the delivery of any goods or payment of their assessed value may be enforced by one or more of the following means—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14] (a) writ of delivery to recover the goods or their assessed value;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14] (b) by order of the court, writ of specific delivery;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14] (c) proceedings for contempt of court under Part 81.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14] (3) An application for an order under paragraph (2)(b) must be made in accordance with Part 23, and must be served on the defendant against whom the judgment or order sought to be enforced was given or made.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14] (4) A writ of specific delivery, and a writ of delivery to recover any goods or their assessed value, may include provision for enforcing the payment of any money adjudged or ordered to be paid by the judgment or order which is to be enforced by the writ.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14] (5) A judgment or order for the payment of the assessed value of any goods may be enforced by the same means as any other judgment or order for the payment of money.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14] (6) This rule applies to writs in aid of writs of delivery.

## Application for permission to issue writ of sequestration

## 83.14A

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14A] (1) An application for permission to issue a writ of sequestration must be made—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14A] (a) to a judge of the Division of the High Court in which the case is proceeding or, in any other case, to a judge of the King’s Bench Division;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14A] (b) by filing an application notice under Part 23.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14A] (2) The application notice must set out the grounds of the application and must be supported by evidence.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14A] (3) The supporting evidence must be by affidavit or affirmation unless and to the extent that the court directs otherwise.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.14A] (4) The application must be served personally on the other party or parties unless the court directs otherwise in accordance with Part 6.

## SECTION IV WARRANTS

## Application for warrant of control or warrant of delivery

## 83.15

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (1)  In this rule, ‘instalment order’ means an order for payment of a sum of money by instalments.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (2) This rule applies in relation to—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (a) warrants of control; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (b) warrants of delivery.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (3) A creditor may apply for a warrant to be issued by filing a request.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (4) A request for a warrant of control or delivery—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (a) may be made without notice; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (b) must be made to—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (i) the County Court hearing centre where the judgment or order which it is sought to enforce was made; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (ii) the County Court hearing centre to which the proceedings have since been transferred.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (5) Subject to paragraph (4)(b)(ii), a request for a warrant of control to enforce a judgment or order made at the Civil National Business Centre must be made to that office.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (6) In the request, the creditor must certify—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (a) the amount remaining due under the judgment or order; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (b) where the order made is an instalment order—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (i) that the whole or part of any instalment due remains unpaid; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (ii) the amount for which the warrant is to be issued.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (7) The court officer may discharge the functions of the District Judge under section 85(2) of the County Courts Act 1984 9 of issuing a warrant.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (8) Unless an instalment order has been made and paragraphs (9) and (10) apply, any warrant issued must be issued for the whole of the sum of money and costs remaining unpaid, and may not be issued for part of the sum.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (9) Where the court has made an instalment order and default has been made in payment of an instalment, then subject to paragraph (10), a warrant of control may be issued for—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (a) the whole of the sum of money and costs then remaining unpaid; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (b) for such part of the sum as the creditor may request, which must not be less than the greater of—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (i) £50; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (ii) the amount of one monthly instalment or, as the case may be, four weekly instalments.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (10) Where an instalment order has been made, no warrant will be issued unless at the time when it is issued—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (a) the whole or part of an instalment which has already become due remains unpaid; and

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.15] (b) any warrant previously issued for part of the sum of money and costs has expired, been satisfied or abandoned.

## Warrant of control or warrant of delivery – opposition by debtor and debtor’s request for transfer

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > Warrant of control or warrant of delivery – opposition by debtor and debtor’s request for transfer] 83.16 The court may, on an application by a debtor who wishes to oppose a request for a warrant of control or warrant of delivery, transfer it to the County Court hearing centre serving the address where the debtor resides or carries on business, or to another court.

## Warrant of control or warrant of delivery – execution of High Court judgment

## 83.17

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.17] (1) Where it is desired to enforce by warrant of control or warrant of delivery—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.17] (a) a judgment or order of the High Court; or

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.17] (b) a judgment, order, decree or award which is or has become enforceable as if it were a judgment of the High Court,

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.17] the request referred to in rule 83.15(3) may be filed in the County Court hearing centre which serves the address where execution is to be levied.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.17] (2) Subject to paragraph (3), any restriction imposed by these rules on the issue of execution will apply as if the judgment, order, decree or award were a judgment or order of the County Court.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.17] (3) Permission to issue execution will not be required if permission has already been given by the High Court.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.17] (4) Notice of the issue of the warrant will be sent by the County Court to the High Court.

## Warrants of control and warrants of delivery – description of parties

## 83.18

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.18] (1) This rule applies where the name or address of the creditor or debtor as given in the request for the issue of the following differs from that person’s name or address in the judgment or order sought to be enforced—

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.18] (a) a warrant of control;

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.18] (b) a warrant of delivery.

[PART 83 – WRITS AND WARRANTS – GENERAL PROVISIONS > 83.18] (2) If the creditor files a witness statement that satisfies the court officer that the name or address as given in the request is applicable to the person concerned, the creditor or the debtor will be described in the warrant as ‘CD of [name and address as given in the request] suing [or sued] as AD of [name and address in the judgment or order]’.
